lines: cfg() { $SYS_PY -c "import json,os,sys; p='$SUB/eval_config.json'; c=json.load(open(p)) if os.path.exists(p) else {}; v=c.get(sys.argv[1]); print('' if v is None else v)" "$1"; }
THINK=$(cfg enable_thinking); case "$THINK" in True|true) THINK=true ;; False|false) THINK=false ;; *) THINK= ;; esac
# Lenient validation: an invalid value is logged and replaced by its default; it never fails the eval.
T0=$TEMP; TEMP=$($SYS_PY -c "import math,sys; v=float(sys.argv[1]); assert math.isfinite(v) and 0<=v<=1.2; print(v)" "$T0" 2>/dev/null) \
+  TOPP=$($SYS_PY -c "import math,sys; v=float(sys.argv[1]); assert math.isfinite(v) and 0<v<=1; print(v)" "$TOPP" 2>/dev/null) \
+  TOPK=$($SYS_PY -c "import sys; v=int(sys.argv[1]); assert v>=1; print(v)" "$TOPK" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { echo "eval_config: top_k=$TOPK invalid (positive int), omitting"; TOPK=; }
case "$PARSER" in json|xml) ;; *) echo "eval_config: parser_name=$PARSER invalid, using json"; PARSER=json ;; esac
-# Model dir: the checkpoint's hf_config + weights, but always the BASE chat template.
+# Per-turn sampling + output cap, forwarded to every LLM call Terminus-2 makes (agent turns and
+# summarization subagents alike) via llm_call_kwargs. This is what actually reaches SGLang:
+# Harbor's LiteLLM chat path otherwise sends only temperature, and model_info's max_output_tokens
+# is metadata only -- it never becomes a request max_tokens, so without this a runaway turn
+# generates until it fills the rest of the 64k context instead of stopping at 8192.
+# temperature still goes through Harbor's own temperature option; top_p/top_k have no Harbor
+# option, so they ride along here (LiteLLM passes both through to SGLang, top_k included).
+# Model dir: the checkpoint's hf_config + weights, serving the checkpoint's own chat template
+# (the base template in reference/ is only a fallback for a checkpoint that ships none).
-# enable_thinking: from eval_config, else the base template's default (2B: off, 4B: on); always pinned into the
-if [ -z "$THINK" ]; then grep -q 'enable_thinking is true' "$TPL" && THINK=false || THINK=true; fi
+# enable_thinking: pin the checkpoint's declared value into the served template. If eval_config
+# does not declare it, serve the template unpinned so its own default applies.
+  echo "eval_config: enable_thinking not set, serving chat template with its own default"
+echo "eval_config: temperature=$TEMP top_p=${TOPP:-<unset>} top_k=${TOPK:-<unset>} max_tokens=$MAX_TOKENS parser=$PARSER thinking=${THINK:-<template default>}"
# The qwen3 reasoning parser assumes thinking; with thinking off it would move the whole answer to reasoning_content.
